issues.legal_issue: A later suit for recovery of possession is not barred by omission of relief in an earlier suit when the two suits are founded on distinct causes of action.
material_facts: An earlier suit sought declaration of title and protection of possession; title was upheld, but an injunction was denied because the plaintiffs were not found to be in possession.
The later suit sought recovery of possession.
The defendants did not establish that the cause of action for the later suit was identical to that of the earlier suit.
issues.conclusion: The later suit was not barred by Order II Rule 2 of the Code of Civil Procedure, and the decree for recovery of possession was affirmed.
issues.legal_principle: Order II Rule 2(1)–(3) requires a plaintiff to include the whole claim and available reliefs arising from the same cause of action, subject to the stated consequences for omission without leave. Under Gurbux Singh v. Bhooralal (1964), the defendant must establish identity of the causes of action and the other elements of the bar; the plea must be proved, including by producing the earlier pleadings, and cannot be presumed. Bengal Waterproof Ltd. v. Bombay Waterproof Manufacturing Co. (1997) reaffirmed the rule. Cause of action comprises the facts necessary to support the right to judgment; the relevant inquiry includes whether the same evidence would maintain both actions. Inacio Martins v. Narayan Hari Naik (1993) and Deva Ram v. Ishwar Chand (1995) support treating a later possession claim as founded on a distinct cause where the earlier suit concerned a different right or a different factual basis for relief. The rule differs from res judicata under Section 11, which concerns matters directly and substantially in issue and finally decided.

rule.if: successive_civil_suits and earlier_suit_sought_possession_protection and later_suit_seeks_recovery_after_loss_of_possession and distinct_causes_of_action

predicates.successive_civil_suits: A plaintiff brought an earlier civil suit and later brought another civil suit against the relevant opposing party.
predicates.earlier_suit_sought_possession_protectio: The earlier suit sought to establish title and protect or confirm the plaintiff's possession.
predicates.later_suit_seeks_recovery_after_loss_of_: The later suit sought recovery of possession after the plaintiff was not in possession.
predicates.distinct_causes_of_action: The facts giving rise to the earlier claim for relief differed from the facts giving rise to the later claim for relief.

issues.definition: When a later civil suit for recovery follows an earlier suit seeking protection of possession and the two suits arise from distinct causes of action, the later suit is not barred for omitting relief from the earlier suit.

issues.legal_issue: A person claiming compensation for improvements may qualify under the applicable tenant definition despite lacking established title, but eligibility depends on the person's good-faith belief and the circumstances and timing of the improvements.
material_facts: The claimant entered into possession as a nephew of the former owner and claimed that he had been put in possession; the court observed that his entry was not by way of encroachment.
He claimed to have made improvements and asserted that he believed he was entitled to make them; he also claimed to have been a lessee.

The claimant's title was rejected, and the lower courts rejected his compensation claim without adequately assessing the relevant good-faith or bona fide belief at the time the improvements were made.

The lower courts noted that the claimant had asserted a claim to be a lessee before making improvements, but the record required factual assessment, including whether improvements were made after the dispute began.
issues.conclusion: The Court expressed no final view on entitlement to compensation and remitted that claim to the trial court for fresh factual assessment under the relevant statutory categories.
issues.legal_principle: Section 2(d) of the Kerala Compensation for Tenants Improvements Act, 1958 contains distinct categories: clause (i) includes a person in possession who in good faith believes himself to be a lessee or another specified interest-holder; clause (ii) addresses a cultivator acting with a bona fide intention to attorn and pay reasonable rent; and clause (iii) includes a person who possesses another's land and makes improvements in the bona fide belief that he is entitled to do so. A claimant's initial entry need not have been by encroachment, but the relevant belief must be assessed factually with reference to when improvements were made. Improvements made after disputes commenced may not satisfy clause (iii).

rule.if: improvement_compensation_claim and claimant_entered_without_encroachment and alleged_improvements and lower_courts_did_not_assess_belief_when_improvements_were_made

predicates.improvement_compensation_claim: A person in possession of land claimed compensation for improvements made to it.
predicates.claimant_entered_without_encroachment: The claimant entered possession in circumstances that were not an encroachment.
predicates.alleged_improvements: The claimant alleged that improvements were made while in possession of the land.
predicates.lower_courts_did_not_assess_belief_when_: The lower courts did not adequately determine whether the claimant held the required good-faith belief when the alleged improvements were made.

issues.definition: When a claimant who entered without encroachment alleges improvements and the lower courts have not assessed the claimant's belief at the time, the improvement claim is returned for that factual assessment.
